dedupe_keys.name: assume agent based electricity markets simulation toolbox

description: ASSUME is an open-source Python toolbox for agent-based simulation of European electricity markets, with a primary focus on the German market setup. Its distinctive feature is the integration of deep reinforcement learning into the bidding strategies of market agents, so that agents adapt their behaviour to market conditions, not following fixed rules, which supports research into new market designs and emergent dynamics. It offers predefined agent representations for demand and generation, including storage, hydrogen plants and industrial units, as plug-and-play modules, and customisable market configurations. It is developed by researchers including Nick Harder, Florian Maurer and Kim K. Miskiw with other contributors, and each release is archived on Zenodo. Coverage is European markets, mainly Germany, while the framework can be configured for other markets. It is installed from PyPI (version 0.6.0 tagged) with source on GitHub under AGPL-3.0-or-later at no cost, requiring Python 3.10 or later. Caveats: reinforcement learning results depend on training settings, and the default data and setups reflect the German market. Simulation uses are agent-based market design studies and optimisation of bidding strategies. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
